name: Deno
tagline: A JavaScript and TypeScript runtime with integrated development tools.
hook: A guide to runtime architecture, native extensions, Cargo-backed JavaScript tests, spec tests, review history, and Rust linting.
summary: Deno's CLAUDE.md explains the CLI, runtime assembly, native extensions, development commands, and test recipes. It shows how spec tests encode commands and expected output, requires incremental review history, and changes lint scope when Rust is touched.

techniques.title: Choose the harness by setup requirements
techniques.body: The guide explicitly warns against running JavaScript and TypeScript unit tests directly with the Deno binary. Cargo owns the setup those tests need.
techniques.quote:
Do NOT run these directly with `./target/debug/deno test` — they depend on the
cargo test harness for correct setup.

techniques.title: Show the spec-test format
techniques.body: A directory contains the command description, input files, and expected output. The example covers both a single command and a sequence of steps, making the custom test format concrete.
techniques.quote:
1. Create a directory in `tests/specs/` with a descriptive name
2. Add a `__test__.jsonc` file describing your test steps
3. Add any input files needed for the test
4. Add `.out` files for expected output (or inline in `__test__.jsonc`)

techniques.title: Explain the output-matching vocabulary
techniques.body: The guide distinguishes wildcards that span lines from those confined to one line, plus unordered blocks and literal character counts. These definitions help keep expectations specific around nondeterministic output.
techniques.quote:
- `[WILDCARD]` : matches 0 or more of any character, like `.*` in regex. this
  can cross newlines
- `[WILDLINE]` : matches 0 or more of any character, ending at the end of a line
- `[WILDCHAR]` - match the next character
- `[WILDCHARS(5)]` - match any of the next 5 characters
- `[UNORDERED_START]` followed by many lines then `[UNORDERED_END]` will match
  the lines in any order (useful for non-deterministic output)
- `[# example]` - line comments start with `[#` and end with `]`

techniques.title: Select lint scope from the changed language
techniques.body: Non-Rust changes use the JavaScript lint path. Rust changes require the full lint command, so verification follows the affected surface.
techniques.quote:
- Before committing, if only non-Rust was changed, make sure to run
  `tools/lint.js --js` and fix any lint errors before committing

techniques.title: Preserve incremental review history
techniques.body: The no-force-push rule explains that changes will be squashed at merge and reviewers need to see follow-up commits. It gives a concrete reason to keep the branch history intact.
techniques.quote:
- When pushing updates to the PR, make sure to never force push. Create as many
  commits as you need, all of them get squashed when the PR is merged, so there
  is no need to rewrite history. This also allows reviewers to see the
  incremental changes you made in response to feedback.

steal: Name the harness responsible for test setup, even when tests use another language.
Include a minimal example of a custom test format.
Explain wildcard semantics before encouraging their use in expected output.
Map changed languages to the appropriate verification commands.
Explain how branch-history rules support the review process.
